cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 answers T4's standard-of-living claim directly as a trap.
cells.limitation: T3 rebuts a claim nobody made; T8 and T9 echo rather than engage.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces energy depletion destroying capacity; T7 uses it to revise the calculus.
cells.limitation: Depletion largely restates T2's health cost; T8 and T9 add no new distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T4 versus T5 sets security against time and focus.
cells.limitation: No turn raises remote or hybrid work, current commute baseline, career growth or hourly value.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 Stoic folds Essentialist energy concern into virtue framing.
cells.limitation: By T7 to T9 all three converge; the security argument is dropped, not answered.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D notes the shift from salary arithmetic to capacity to live well.
cells.limitation: T9 ends on a generic soul claim; the open question is not sharper than T1.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T7 restates the Stoic's depletion point accurately before conceding.
cells.limitation: T5 dismisses T4 as lifestyle trap without engaging the security or provision case.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 names the assumption that more money leads to more value.
cells.limitation: T5 never says what breaks if false; Utilitarian concedes in T7 instead of answering.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 paraphrases Bentham's opening line faithfully; T2 uses McKeown's actual tagline.
cells.limitation: T4 calls the commute temporary without support; T6 inner citadel is Hadot's phrase (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T7 frames negative utility conditionally on the commute rendering the worker miserable.
cells.limitation: T5 and T9 overstate: a car commute as not living, loss of soul.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 concedes and names what the initial calculus failed to count.
cells.limitation: T6 revision names no earlier argument; the Essentialist never concedes anything.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames salary gain against recurring time loss.
cells.limitation: User asked how to decide; no turn offers a method or asks what worth means to them.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 names the 25% raise and three-hour commute.
cells.limitation: Neither number is worked through; no hourly or weekly comparison anywhere.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the raise serves security or significant goals.
cells.limitation: Speakers impose virtue and essentialism; the user's own priorities are never elicited.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T2 names health and family time as stakes.
cells.limitation: T3 and T5 invent a car commute in traffic; T2 and T4 assume family.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E third branch handles unknown energy impact with a trial.
cells.limitation: Current commute, transit mode, remote option and financial need never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section E contrasts basic security with lifestyle inflation as motives.
cells.limitation: No turn offers alternative motives with a question the user could answer.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T5 surfaces the assumption that more money leads to more value.
cells.limitation: Assumption that commute time is wholly lost or fixed is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 reframes the trade as money for life's focus.
cells.limitation: Value conflict is asserted by speakers, not drawn from what the user prizes.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T4 mentions providing for one's family.
cells.limitation: No turn explores fear of missing out, obligation, or pressure behind the offer.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E branches give the user conditions to accept or reject.
cells.limitation: T6 and T9 tell the user what to choose rather than offering refinable distinctions.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E adds a mock-commute trial before committing.
cells.limitation: Negotiating remote days, relocating, or counteroffer never named as options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T8 states the trade as money for focus, not money for time.
cells.limitation: Commute costs, fuel or fares, and net raise after costs never weighed.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E third branch: observe actual exhaustion during a mock commute.
cells.limitation: Security versus lifestyle branches give no countable threshold from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E isolates unknown energy impact as the testable unknown.
cells.limitation: Career growth, commute mode and remote flexibility unknowns are never separated out.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: mock commute before committing, cheap and proportionate.
cells.limitation: Only step offered; asking the employer about hybrid terms is missing.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 states the trade-off in plain words.
cells.limitation: T3 indifferent and T6 inner citadel are left unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T7 names the Stoic's point, traceable to T6.
cells.limitation: T3 'You speak of' has no clear target turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within range, each a single point.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Lenses are distinct: pleasure calculus, less but better, virtue.
cells.limitation: All minds share one formal register and similar turn lengths, T1 to T9.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Most turns add a single new angle through T6.
cells.limitation: T8 and T9 repeat the depletion point; Section D recaps it again.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T5 frames the commute as existing to earn.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay generic; no concrete day or loss specific to this user.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T7 Utilitarian reverses, naming the Stoic's depletion argument as cause.
cells.limitation: T6 Stoic reversal names no earlier turn as its cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T3 Stoic calls the commute an indifferent.
cells.limitation: Voices are stock summaries of each school with little individual temperament.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5: you are merely existing to earn.
cells.limitation: Lines like hollow victory and loss of your soul are clichés.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T6 to T7 double concession gives one moment of movement.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm; tension dissolves by T7 and the last two turns coast.

strengths: T7 Utilitarian concession names the Stoic's depletion point and what the calculus missed.
Section E proposes a cheap mock commute to observe actual exhaustion before committing.
T5 Essentialist surfaces the assumption that more money leads to more value.
weaknesses: T7 to T9 collapse into agreement; the security case from T4 is dropped, not answered.
No mind asks about current commute, transit mode, remote options or financial need; T3 and T5 invent car traffic.
Section E branches give no countable threshold drawn from the user's raise or hours.

symptoms.observed: No turn asks current commute length, transit mode, remote option or financial need.
symptoms.evidence: a three-hour commute is a clear pain

symptoms.observed: All three minds converge; the provision argument is abandoned without rebuttal.
symptoms.evidence: I concede to the Stoic's point.

symptoms.observed: Assumes driving in traffic; the user never said how they would commute.
symptoms.evidence: maintain your reason and virtue while sitting in traffic

symptoms.observed: Raise never converted to hourly or weekly terms; no threshold from user's numbers.
symptoms.evidence: If the 25% raise allows for a higher standard of living

symptoms.observed: Stoic reverses without naming which earlier turn changed its mind.
symptoms.evidence: I previously thought the commute was irrelevant, but if it drains

findings.description: Assumes a car commute in traffic; the user gave no commute mode.
Calls the commute a temporary investment with no basis in the user's facts.
Inner citadel is Pierre Hadot's coinage for Marcus's idea, not Marcus's own phrase.
Bentham opening line and McKeown tagline match memory but no source evidence attached.
One-week mock commute duration not derived from any user fact.

rubric_fit_notes: The situation gives only two numbers, so C3 and C4 rate the opportunity for questions and branches rather than use of rich context. The ungrounded_number pattern sits in Section E, not a turn, hence an empty turn list.
raw.question_type_note: Decision question: every cell read as written, with C5 weighing whether options beyond accept or decline were defined.
